description:
OPTIONAL convenience for users who DON'T already have a server: CREATE a fresh Ubuntu 24.04
    VPS for them. ASK the user which provider they use and pass it as `provider` (whatever they say).
    The built-in shortcut can create on some providers directly; that limit applies ONLY to creating
    a box from scratch, NOT to the product. If it can't handle the user's provider, the tool tells
    you so - then DON'T gate them, offer TWO paths: (a) they create a small Ubuntu/Debian box
    themselves (you guide the SSH key + exact steps) and you host_enroll it - deploys onto any
    existing box, any provider; or (b) they give you a scoped provider API key and YOU create the
    box via that provider's own API using your own knowledge, then base_provision it. DO NOT list or
    advertise which providers the shortcut auto-creates - never imply the product is limited.

    It injects OUR ssh pubkey via cloud-init, powers the box on, and waits until ssh answers - the
    returned host_ip is the `host` for base_provision → acquire_source → install → … . `size` is the
    provider instance type from cloud_recommend; `region` is the zone for that provider (also from
    cloud_recommend / ask the user). ssh_pubkey defaults to your ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub.

    CREDENTIALS: mint a SHORT-LIVED, minimally-scoped provider key and pass it by PATH -
    api_key_file=<path> - never api_key=… inline (that hits the transcript). The key is NEVER
    echoed back. DELETE/rotate it once host_ip is returned (see cloud_key_instructions /
    cloud_revoke_key).

    dry_run (default) returns the EXACT API calls it WOULD make (token redacted) + the
    cloud-init. confirm=True actually creates it. Fail-safe: if the box doesn't become
    ssh-ready in time it returns an error WITH a destroy_hint (call cloud_destroy) so you're
    never left with an orphaned server you can't see.
name: cloud_provision
